title: Drop the 15-month rise in the bank surcharge
name: Drop the 15-month rise in the bank surcharge
headline: Drop the bank surcharge rise. Costs £0.9bn in 2027-28, nothing by 2029-30.
description: The bank surcharge doubles from 3% to 6% for the 15 months from January 2027 to March 2028, to pay for the Budget’s help with bills. Switch this on to drop the rise. It raises nothing by 2029-30, so this moves the earlier years, not the target year.

baselinePolicy.text: The bank surcharge is 6% from 1 January 2027 to 31 March 2028, then 3% again (Table 6.1 line 55).

source.quote: increasing the combined rate of Corporation Tax and Banking Surcharge on affected profits from 28 per cent to 31 per cent for a 15 month period

alreadyIncludes: The bank surcharge is 6% from 1 January 2027 to 31 March 2028, then 3% again (Table 6.1 line 55).

lines.title: Bank Surcharge: Temporarily increase the Bank Corporation Tax Surcharge rate from 3% to 6%, to fund breathing space measures for households, for 15 months from 1 January 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.

interactions.text: Both move the surcharge: the two-point rise here is costed on the 3% rate, which the Budget’s 6% already doubles until March 2028.
